findings.text: Spotify's API rate limit is calculated based on the number of calls that your app makes to Spotify in a rolling 30 second window.
findings.quote: Spotify's API rate limit is calculated based on the number of calls that your app makes to Spotify in a rolling 30 second window.

findings.text: If your app makes a lot of Web API requests in a short period of time then it may receive a 429 error response from Spotify.
findings.quote:
If your app makes a lot of Web API requests in a short period of time then it
may receive a 429 error response from Spotify. This indicates that your app has
reached our Web API rate limit.

findings.text: Apps in development mode have quota restrictions that differ from standard rate limits.
findings.quote:
Note that development mode apps also have
quota restrictions which
have a different enforcement mechanism than rate limits.

findings.text: Apply for extended quota mode by opening the app detail page in the Developer Dashboard and tapping the Request Extension link.
findings.quote:
You can apply for a quota extension by opening your app detail page in the Developer
Dashboard and tapping on the Request Extension link.

findings.text: You can create up to 25 apps per developer account.
findings.quote: You can create up to 25 apps per developer account.

findings.text: Go to your Dashboard and click on the Create an App button.
findings.quote: To create an app, go to your Dashboard and click on the Create an App button to open the following dialog box:

findings.text: Enter an App Name and App Description, tick the Developer Terms of Service checkbox, and click CREATE.
findings.quote: Enter an App Name and App Description of your choice (they will be displayed to the user on the grant screen), put a tick in the Developer Terms of Service checkbox and finally click on CREATE.

findings.text: Click on Edit Settings to view and update your app settings.
findings.quote: It is time to configure our app. Click on Edit Settings to view and update your app settings.

findings.text: Add a web domain or URL to the Website field.
findings.quote: Add a web domain or URL to the Website field. This will help users to obtain more information about your application.

findings.text: Enter one or more addresses in Redirect URIs to allowlist with Spotify.
findings.quote: In Redirect URIs enter one or more addresses that you want to allowlist with Spotify. This URI enables the Spotify authentication service to automatically invoke your app every time the user logs in (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8080)

findings.text: Click on SAVE after updating app settings.
findings.quote: Once you have finished updating the app settings, click on SAVE.

findings.text: Never reveal your client secret key publicly.
findings.quote: Always store the client secret key securely; never reveal it publicly!

findings.text: Access tokens are valid for 1 hour.
findings.quote: The response will return an access token valid for 1 hour:

findings.text: The authorization process requires a client ID and a client secret.
findings.quote: The authorization process requires valid client credentials: a client ID and a client secret. You can follow the Apps guide to learn how to generate them.

findings.text: The authorization code flow is recommended for long-running server-side applications that can safely store a client secret.
findings.quote: If you are developing a long-running application (e.g. web app running on the server) that can refresh access tokens and request user authorization again when needed, and the client secret can be safely stored, then the authorization code flow is the recommended choice.

findings.text: The authorization code with PKCE flow is recommended for desktop, mobile, or browser-based apps where storing a client secret is not safe.
findings.quote: In scenarios where storing the client secret is not safe (e.g. desktop, mobile apps or JavaScript web apps running in the browser), you can use the authorization code with PKCE, as it provides protection against attacks where the authorization code may be intercepted.

findings.text: The Client credentials flow is typically used for backend applications like CLIs or daemons that do not require user authorization.
findings.quote: For some applications running on the backend, such as CLIs or daemons, the system authenticates and authorizes the app rather than a user. For these scenarios, Client credentials is the typical choice.

findings.text: A redirect URI must be specified when creating an app.
findings.quote: When you create an app, you need to specify a redirect URI. This is the URI to which Spotify redirects the user after they have granted or denied permission to your app.

findings.text: Using localhost as a redirect URI is not allowed.
findings.quote: localhost is not allowed as redirect URI.

findings.text: Redirect URIs must use HTTPS unless using a loopback address.
findings.quote: Use HTTPS for your redirect URI, unless you are using a loopback address, when HTTP is permitted.

findings.text: Apps start in development mode and can move to extended quota mode for a wider audience.
